To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
lentiviral transduction of a potent short hairpin RNA against CCR5 in human CD34(+) stem/progenitor cells resulted in stable knockdown of CCR5 expression and HIV-1 coreceptors in human cells in vivo.
lentiviral delivery of shRNA to human HPSCs can stably knock down CCR5 expression systemically, and that this strategy may provide a novel approach to control HIV-1 infection.

lentiviral delivery of a highly efficient CCR5 short hairpin RNA into human hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells stably knocked down CCR5 expression, which was effective against CCR5 tropism HIV-1 infection, in systemic lymphoid tissue in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new strategy to inhibit HIV-1 infection by using a lentiviral vector to knockdown CCR5 expression.
the development of a new therapeutic strategy to control HIV-1 infection by targeting CCR5 expression.
the development of a novel gene therapy strategy for HIV-1 infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lentiviral vector-mediated shRNA delivery into human HPSC is a promising approach to inhibit HIV-1 infection.
this work provides proof of concept that shRNA-mediated CRR5 knockdown can be achieved in a humanized mouse model, with the potential to be applied for HIV-1 gene therapy.
the shRNA against CRR5 is a promising approach for the prevention and treatment of HIV/AIDS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel strategy of CCR5 gene knockdown in the humanized BLT mouse model by shRNA delivered by lentiviral vectors, which is a promising approach for controlling HIV- 1 infection.
we successfully developed an effective and safe gene therapy for HIV-1 infection by targeting the CCR5 coreceptor.
we have successfully established a humanized bone-marrow/liver/thymic (BLT) mice model with stable knockdown of CCR5 by short hairpin RNA in systemic lymphoid tissue.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the human BLT model is a useful tool for evaluating lentiviral vector-mediated gene transfer in human hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells and for assessing the efficacy of gene silencing in human lymphoid organs.
the humanized BLT model is useful to evaluate the efficacy of CCR5 knock-down in systemic lymphoid tissue, and the lentiviral vector system is a promising tool for gene therapy in humans.
the shRNA-mediated CCCR5 knockdown in humanized BLT mice could be used for the development of novel anti-HIV-1 gene therapy strategies in humans.
